question: After refreshing this branch against current `main`, does the plugin-registry owner accept the behavioral-equivalence evidence for the moved lifecycle, rollback, and runtime authorization paths?
rationale: The branch is a very broad internal refactor of compatibility- and security-sensitive plugin infrastructure, carries a protected maintainer label, and has no narrow mechanical defect that automation can resolve instead of owner review.

options.title: Refresh and approve
options.body: Rebase the branch, rerun the focused registry and boundary proof, and approve after owner inspection confirms behavior equivalence.

options.title: Narrow the refactor
options.body: Split the API/runtime authorization movement from the domain registrar extraction if the combined review surface is too large to validate safely.

options.title: Pause the decomposition
options.body: Leave the linked issue open and close this branch if maintainers no longer want to absorb the broad refactor risk.

recommendation.title: Refresh and approve
recommendation.body: Rebase the branch, rerun the focused registry and boundary proof, and approve after owner inspection confirms behavior equivalence.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence identifies this person as the issue author, PR assignee, implementation author, and coordinator of the maintainer-requested registry refactor.
